Class 1 · Chapter 5 of 8

Measure length and weight

Compare fairly and measure with equal units.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Shapes and solid objects. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can measure with equal units.
  • I can compare weights.
  • I can choose a sensible unit.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 3

Start at zero

To measure length, put one end at zero.

Read the number at the other end. This pencil is 6 units long.

Screen 2 of 3

Units must be equal

Count with units that are all the same size.

If the units are different sizes, the answer is not fair.

Screen 3 of 3

Weigh on a balance

The heavier side goes down.

When both sides weigh the same, the balance is level.

Words to know
unit
A fixed size we count with, like a paper clip or a cube.
length
How long something is from end to end.
heavier
Pushes down harder on a balance.

For parents

What your child learns

Measuring means counting equal units placed end to end with no gaps. We choose a unit that fits the thing: metres for a rope, grams for a small mass. A level balance means both sides weigh the same.

A common slip

Children may leave gaps or overlap units, or choose a tiny unit for a long thing. Start at zero and place units edge to edge. Ask if the unit fits the size.

5-minute home activity: Measure with units

  1. Measure a table with the same pencil placed end to end.
  2. Count the pencils with no gaps.
  3. Measure a book with paper clips.
  4. Say which unit you would use for a long rope.
